WHATWG HTML — landmarks and semantics (digest)
Landmarks are regions of a page that represent navigable content
sections. They are conveyed to assistive technology.

Page structure:
- header (banner): introductory content, typically the masthead
- nav: set of navigation links
- main: the main content of the document
- footer (contentinfo): about the page or site
- aside: tangentially related content
- section: a thematic grouping of content, usually with a heading
- article: a self-contained composition (that could stand alone)
- form: a region that contains a form
- search: a region with site search functionality

The doc element:
- The main element must not be used more than once per document,
  unless it is hidden.
- Landmark elements must have an accessible name when there is more
  than one of the same type.
- The header and footer elements are not landmark regions when their
  nearest ancestor sectioning content is the body.

ARIA roles refine semantics:
- role=banner, role=navigation, role=main, role=contentinfo
- role=region with an accessible name for generic regions
- role=search for search regions
- role=complementary for aside content

Assistive technology exposes landmarks for quick navigation: prefer
native elements over divs with ARIA roles, and give each landmark a
labelled heading or aria-label when the content does not already
identify the region.
